references.text: Abraham explains his behavior by stating that there is no fear of God in the place – a direct parallel to Joseph, who justifies his action with his own fear of God.
God confirms that Abraham fears Him after he was willing to sacrifice Isaac. This is a key text about the fear of God in Genesis.
The midwives feared God and acted righteously – an example of how the fear of God motivates ethical behavior, as Joseph demonstrates here.
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom – this underscores the importance of the fear of God that Joseph expresses.
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge – a wisdom text that supports Joseph's fear of God as the foundation for righteous action.
Abraham's faith and fear of God when he was willing to sacrifice Isaac, which illuminates the theme of the fear of God expressed by Joseph.
Both verses show how Joseph uses his 'fear of God' as a theological basis to overcome human fear and exercise grace.
It illustrates how 'the fear of God' functions as a double-edged sword: both a disciplinary warning and a source of mercy.
A typological parallel where 'the third day' in Joseph's story serves as a precursor to the resurrection day.
